note: Drop clips in public/sign/ named after each entry id and run `npm run sign:sync`. Until a clip exists the entry shows a clearly labelled placeholder. See content/ISL-CLIPS.md.

signVideoCredit.text: Sign videos from Spread the Sign, © European Sign Language Centre. Used with permission.
signVideoCredit.note: Shown under every clip that does not set its own credit. Record the permission itself in content/ISL-CLIPS.md — who granted it, when, and what it covers. If a clip comes from a different source, set `credit` on that entry instead; it wins over this. If you film your own and need no attribution, set appliesToUnattributed to false.

entries.definition: What people use to buy things. In India we use rupees.
entries.example: A snack costs ₹20. You give the shop ₹20 in money.

entries.definition: The money used in India. Its sign is ₹.
entries.example: A ₹100 note is one hundred rupees.

entries.definition: Money made of metal. It is round and small.
entries.example: India has ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20 coins.

entries.definition: Money made of paper.
entries.example: A ₹500 note is worth more than a ₹10 coin.

entries.definition: How much money a thing costs.
entries.example: The price of the notebook is ₹40.

entries.definition: To use money to buy something.
entries.example: She spent ₹20 on a snack.

entries.definition: To keep money now so you can use it later.
entries.example: He saves ₹10 every week for a cricket ball.

entries.definition: Something you must have to stay well, like food or a home.
entries.example: Clean water is a need.

entries.definition: Something nice to have, but you can live without it.
entries.example: A new toy is a want.

entries.definition: A written plan for your money. It shows money in and money out.
entries.example: Her budget gives ₹100 to snacks each month.

entries.definition: Money that comes to you, usually from work.
entries.example: His income is ₹300 of pocket money each month.

entries.definition: Money that goes out when you buy something.
entries.example: Bus fare of ₹15 is a daily expense.

entries.definition: A thing you are saving for, with a price and a date.
entries.example: My goal is ₹4000 for a bicycle by next June.

entries.definition: A safe place that keeps your money and records how much is yours.
entries.example: She keeps her savings at a bank near school.

entries.definition: Your own record at a bank. It shows the money that belongs to you.
entries.example: He opened an account with his mother.

entries.definition: Putting money into your bank account.
entries.example: She made a deposit of ₹500.

entries.definition: Taking money out of your bank account.
entries.example: He made a withdrawal of ₹200 at the ATM.

entries.definition: The amount of money in your account right now.
entries.example: Her balance is ₹1,250.

entries.definition: A machine that gives you cash from your account. You need a card and a PIN.
entries.example: He took ₹500 from the ATM.

entries.definition: Extra money. A bank pays you interest on savings. You pay interest when you borrow.
entries.example: ₹1000 at 5 percent earns ₹50 of interest in one year.

entries.definition: Interest paid on your money and on the interest you already earned.
entries.example: Money left for many years grows faster with compound interest.

entries.definition: A fixed amount of money paid for work, every month.
entries.example: His salary arrives on the first day of the month.

entries.definition: The money left after you take costs away from sales.
entries.example: Sales ₹500 minus costs ₹300 is ₹200 profit.

entries.definition: Money paid to the government. It pays for roads, hospitals and schools.
entries.example: Income tax is taken out before your salary reaches you.

entries.definition: A secret number that proves a card or account is yours. Never share it.
entries.example: She types her PIN at the ATM, hiding the keypad.

entries.definition: A one time password sent to your phone. A real bank will never ask you for it.
entries.example: A caller asked for his OTP. He refused and hung up.

entries.definition: A trick used to take your money.
entries.example: A message about a prize she never entered was a scam.

entries.definition: A fake message that copies a real company to steal your details.
entries.example: The email used the bank's logo, but the address was wrong.

entries.definition: A way to send money from a phone in India. You enter a PIN only to send money.
entries.example: He paid the shop ₹60 using UPI.

entries.definition: Prices slowly going up over time. Each rupee buys a little less.
entries.example: A snack was ₹20 last year. Now it is ₹24.
